author: Leena Nasir
title: En Vogue Star Dawn Robinson Says She's Homeless | The Daily Caller
text:
Dawn Robinson, member of the hit ’90s girl group En Vogue, said she is homeless and has been living in her car for three years.
Robinson was best known as a singer of the top performing R&B group that took the 90s by storm. She told fans about how she went from superstardom to homelessness Tuesday on her YouTube channel in a video titled “Your New Life is in the Scary.”
The famous singer said she lived with her parents back in 2020 but began facing troubles with her mother. She received a call from her manager promising a better life in Los Angeles and accepted the offer. Robinson soon discovered the situation was less than ideal and researched the culture of living in her car.
“There’s a whole community of people that live in their cars,” she said. “I loved what I was seeing.”
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=s7MU-2VBN2w
The famous singer said she has learned to adapt to the unique living conditions, but admitted she never imagined this would be part of her life’s journey.
Robinson told fans she uses her gym membership to facilitate showers. The singer also put the spotlight on her ex-boyfriend’s mother, her personal assistant Niecy, her brother Evin and Klymaxx singer Joyce Irby for supporting her through this unexpected phase in her life, according to TMZ.
She declared she began living in her car March 9, 2022 and admitted “that first night was scary.”
“As I got to know what to do in my car and how to do it, like how to cover my windows and um you know you don’t talk to certain people — you’re careful of telling people that you’re alone, as a woman especially — and I’m a celebrity,” she said.
SANTA MONICA, CALIFORNIA – OCTOBER 10: Dawn Robinson, Terry Ellis, Maxine Jones, Rhona Bennett, and Cindy Herron of En Vogue perform onstage during City Of Hope Spirit Of Life Gala 2019 on October 10, 2019 in Santa Monica, California. (Photo by Charley Gallay/Getty Images for City of Hope)
Robinson said she faced some trouble with her vehicle, but overall was happy with her choice.
“I felt free. That was a sense of freedom that I had,” she said.
“I felt like I was on a camping trip. I just felt like it was the right thing to do. I didn’t regret it,” the En Vogue singer told her fans.
“You know, a lot of celebrities have slept in their cars,” she said, before drawing on Marvin Gaye as an example.
LOS ANGELES – DECEMBER 1993: The women of soul R&B group En Vogue pose for a portrait in December 1993 in Los Angeles, California. (Photo by Aaron Rapoport/Corbis/Getty Images)
Robinson clarified, “This is not like, oh my God, poor Dawn — she’s living in her car and it’s terrible.”
“I’m learning about who I am, I’m learning myself as a person, as a woman. I am documenting this whole adventure — it’s an adventure, you guys, it’s a journey,” she said.
She went on to say she was “glad” she choose this lifestyle.
“I needed to go through this fire,” Robinson told her fans.
American vocal girl group En Vogue arriving at the the Seventh Annual Soul Train Music Awards at the Shrine Auditorium in Los Angeles, California, 9th March 1993. L – R: Cindy Herron, Maxine Jones, Terry Ellis, Dawn Robinson. (Photo by Vinnie Zuffante/Getty Images)
American vocal girl group En Vogue at the 20th Annual American Music Awards with their ‘Favorite Soul/R&B Album’ award won for ‘Funky Divas’, Shrine Auditorium, Los Angeles, California, 25th January 1993. L – R: Dawn Robinson, Maxine Jones, Terry Ellis, Cindy Herron. (Photo by Vinnie Zuffante/Getty Images)
“I’m definitely, I’m in the trenches of this right now and I’m like, I wouldn’t trade my experiences and what I’ve gone through for the world,” she said. “I needed to do this alone and without everybody’s judgment or opinions and all of that stuff. I needed to do this for me.” (RELATED: Disney Child Star Jack Veal Pleads For Help Claiming He’s Homeless And Was Abused)
En Vogue sold millions of records worldwide and topped the Billboard charts at the height of the group’s fame. Robinson stepped away from the group in 1997. She claimed “they kicked me out” in a 2020 interview with You Know I Got Soul.
